title: TSMC October Revenue Jumps 59.7% as Growth Accelerates
gist: TSMC's October 2026 revenue hit NT$586.89B, up 14.7% MoM and 59.7% YoY, outpacing its 43.3% year-to-date growth and giving a strong start toward Q4 guidance of US$52.3-54.3B, though the report says nothing about margins.

insights.claim: TSMC October 2026 consolidated revenue was NT$586.89 billion, up 14.7% from September 2026 and 59.7% from October 2025.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Monthly revenue reaccelerating to ~60% YoY confirms AI-driven foundry demand is still strengthening into Q4 2026.
insights.quote: Consolidated revenue reached NT$586.89 billion, rising 14.7% from September and 59.7% from October 2025.

insights.claim: TSMC revenue for January-October 2026 totaled NT$4,485.62 billion, up 43.3% year over year, meaning October's 59.7% YoY growth exceeded the cumulative run-rate.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Growth accelerating above the YTD average signals momentum is building, not fading, entering Q4.

insights.claim: TSMC's October 2026 revenue was roughly NT$75 billion higher than September's.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A sequential step-up of this size at the start of Q4 suggests the 2nm ramp is contributing early.

insights.claim: TSMC guided Q4 2026 revenue to US$52.3-54.3 billion at an assumed NT$31.8 per US dollar, and October's result is a strong opening contribution toward that range.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Track November/December monthly prints and the TWD/USD rate to gauge a beat versus the top of guidance.

insights.claim: TSMC management expected continued Q4 2026 demand for leading-edge nodes, including a steep production ramp of its 2 nanometer technology.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The 2nm ramp is the key driver to watch for mix and pricing tailwinds.

insights.claim: Advanced technologies (7nm and below) represented 79% of TSMC's Q3 2026 wafer revenue.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Leading-edge concentration underpins TSMC's pricing power and its leverage to AI accelerator demand.

insights.claim: TSMC's monthly revenue releases disclose no earnings, operating costs, margins, or customer/application/node breakdown, so strong revenue growth alone cannot show whether profitability improved at the same pace.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Don't extrapolate revenue strength to margins; wait for the quarterly report for mix and gross margin.
